chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Two rak'ahs of the Sunnah are not prayed in any place except in Medina.
He said: 'They are prayed in the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) on the day of Eid, before going out to the prayer ground; this is not [done] except in Medina.
Because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed it [there].'

key_terms.الْعِيدِ: Eid (festival, specifically Eid al-Fitr or Eid al-Adha)
key_terms.الْمُصَلَّى: The prayer ground (open area for Eid prayers)
key_terms.بِالْمَدِينَةِ: In Medina (specifically referring to the city of the Prophet)
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Messenger (Prophet's Mosque)

ai.seo_question: Where and when should the two-rak'ah Eid Sunnah prayer be performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the specific Sunnah of performing two rak'ahs in the Prophet's Mosque (Masjid al-Nabawi) before departing for the Eid prayer ground, a practice uniquely preserved in Medina as the direct tradition of the Messenger of Allah. While other schools may generalize this prayer, Shia scholarship emphasizes its location-specific nature, linking the ritual directly to the sanctity of the Prophet's physical presence and his established custom in that city.
